samples.summary: Read-only write gate for image mutation lives in the leaf, downstream of an entry point that deliberately runs before the enforced readOnly check
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` dispatches to `imageKeyHandler` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:854, i.e. *before* its own read-only early-return at text-editor.ts:883. The change therefore relies on each mutating branch inside the handler re-declaring the gate itself — here `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2243 `if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;`). I traced every branch of the new handler (Escape, Delete/Backspace, arrows, mod+c/mod+x, catch-all) and only Delete/Backspace mutates, so there is no live bypass today; `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1219) also gates read-only before reaching `imageDeleteHandler`. The weakness is structural: the authorization decision is made after dispatch, in a helper that also happens to be exported to `TextEditor` as `imageDeleteHandler`, so any future branch added to `imageKeyHandler` (or any other caller wiring that hook) silently escapes the gate. This matters more than usual here because the server-side write gate is off by default: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97 returns allow whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (shadow mode, the documented default in packages/backend/README.md:111), so for anonymous share-link viewers (`readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:278) this client-side check is in practice the only thing stopping a CRDT write. Preferred shape: gate once at the dispatch site (skip/limit `imageKeyHandler` when `this.readOnly`) rather than per-branch.

samples.summary: `selectImageAt` has no read-only guard, and it is the only way the newly-added read-only-sensitive image hooks can be reached in a viewer session
samples.evidence: The mouse path that normally creates an image selection bails in read-only (`handleImageMouseDown`, editor.ts:2454 `if (readOnly) return;`), but the public `EditorAPI.selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3639) does not, so a caller can establish `selectedImage` in a read-only editor — which is exactly the precondition the diff's new `imageSelectionProvider` / `imageDeleteHandler` / Delete-Backspace branch consume. Nothing in the frontend calls it today (grep for `selectImageAt|clearImageSelection|getSelectedImage` under packages/frontend/src returned no matches), and the diff's own test uses it precisely to reach the read-only delete path, so this is currently only a defence-in-depth gap rather than an exploit. Worth either guarding the selection API in read-only or documenting that every consumer of `selectedImage` must re-check `readOnly`.
searchedFor: grep readOnly in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts (lines 2454, 2558, 2566, 3591, 3665 all guarded)

samples.summary: Image `src` from an untrusted clipboard payload is never scheme/host-validated before becoming a live network request, and this change adds a new producer for that path
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` (text-editor.ts:1261) is documented as round-tripping 'through the ordinary `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` path with no special case at the other end'. On the read side, `sanitizeImageData` (clipboard.ts:110-128) accepts any string as `src` — unlike `href`, which every consumer gates with `isSafeUrl` (text-editor.ts:1624, text-editor.ts:1966, pdf-painter.ts:834, docs-link-popover.tsx:183). The pasted value reaches `img.src = src` unfiltered at packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:71. Vector: a hostile page puts its own `application/x-waffledocs` JSON on the system clipboard from its `copy` handler with `style.image.src = 'https://attacker/beacon?id=…'`; the victim pastes into a doc, the reference is written into the shared CRDT, and every collaborator's browser then fetches the attacker URL on render (read receipts / IP + UA disclosure). Pre-existing (the diff does not touch the paste side) and only a beacon, not script execution, since `javascript:` is inert as an `` src — hence low confidence and minor severity; flagged because the change newly relies on and documents this path.

samples.summary: The new plain-text clipboard flavour for an image is the alt text, which defaults to the uploader's original local filename
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` sets `text/plain` to `image.alt ?? ''` (text-editor.ts:1271). `alt` is populated with `file.name` on every uploaded image (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:66, `alt: file.name`). So Cmd/Ctrl+C over a click-selected image — a path that previously wrote nothing at all — now puts the original local filename on the system clipboard, where the next paste target (any app or page the user pastes into) reads it. Filenames routinely carry sensitive context ('Q3-layoffs-draft.png'). User-initiated and low impact, but it is a new outbound flavour of a value the user did not type.

samples.summary: `preventDefault()` is called before the clipboard write, so a throw inside `writeImageToClipboard` still clears the user's system clipboard — the hazard the `findBlock` guard was added for is only half-closed
samples.evidence: handleCopy's new image branch does `e.preventDefault();` (text-editor.ts:1195) and only then `writeImageToClipboard`, whose `serializeClipboard`/`JSON.stringify` can throw (e.g. a very large data-URL `src`). The provider was deliberately written with the non-throwing `findBlock` (editor.ts:2262) precisely because 'a throw would escape the listener and let the default copy wipe the user's system clipboard' — but that reasoning stops at the lookup and does not cover the write that follows the `preventDefault()`. Availability/data-loss of clipboard contents rather than a confidentiality or authorization defect; wrapping the write in try/catch (or building the payload string before `preventDefault`) would close it.

samples.summary: Context menu relaxes a permission-conditioned control (`showCopy` no longer requires `!readOnly`) — verified not to be a policy bypass
samples.evidence: `showCopy = hasSelection` (docs-context-menu.tsx:181) drops the previous `&& !readOnly`, and `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection` (line 80) opens the menu for viewers. `readOnly` is `role === 'viewer'` for share links (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152/278/318/368/395/683). I searched the repo for any copy-restriction policy (`disableCopy|allowCopy|canCopy|preventCopy|copyProtect|copyDisabled`) and found none, and keyboard ⌘C is already deliberately allowed in read-only (text-editor.ts:896-898), so this grants a viewer no capability they did not already have and `editor.copy()` (editor.ts:3333) is non-mutating. Recorded only because it is a deliberate loosening of a `readOnly`-conditioned UI gate; no action needed unless a 'view without copy' role is ever introduced.
